clue.text: Offers of work put in writing by head of section

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for writing

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word section

explanation.surface: Job offers are confirmed in a letter from the section head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offers' looks like a plural noun, as in offers of work, but it is the verb; 'put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a plan or suggestion is to propose it, a synonym of offering.

clue.text: Type of cat trailing cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A breed of cat that follows a cuckoo around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like a bird the cat is chasing, but it means mad and signals an anagram of TRAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringtail cat is a small raccoon relative of North America with a banded tail.

clue.text: Ultimately, father's prepared to join in risky activities at home

indicators.note: to join in tells us the pieces go inside the word for risky

parts.note: parlous means dangerous or precarious

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of father

parts.note: game means willing or ready, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: A father is ready to take part in dangerous pursuits around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risky activities' wants to be the definition, but 'risky' alone is the container that 'to join in' opens. The 's on father's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades and similar indoor pastimes played in the sitting room are the classic examples of these.

clue.text: Part of film showing different view of queens' college after vacation

indicators.note: a different view of the letters means rearranging them
vacation means emptying, so the word college loses all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A movie scene presenting a new angle on a Cambridge college once term has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' suggests a holiday from Queens' College, Cambridge, but it means emptying; 'different view of' is the anagram signal. University vacations are the breaks between terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is a run of connected shots or scenes forming one episode in a movie.

clue.text: Restrict journalist probing sleaze, half of it continuously censored

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so one piece goes into another
one unbroken half of the word sleaze is cut away, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: a hack is a slang word for a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter investigating corruption finds half the story constantly cut by censors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of it continuously censored' removes AZE, one unbroken half of the word, leaving three letters for 'probing' to open.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetter someone, literally or figuratively, is to restrict their movement.

clue.text: Beautician's business is growing

definitions.meaning: removing hair by applying hot wax is work done at a beauty salon
increasing in size, as the moon does before it is full

explanation.definitionFit: Hair removal with hot wax is a salon treatment; the moon is said to wax as it gets bigger.

clue.text: Affected male wearing hat

indicators.note: the male is wearing the hat, so the hat goes round him

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A pretentious man in a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes behaviour that is theatrical, exaggerated and mannered.

clue.text: Number of animals outside a lair

indicators.note: outside tells us one word goes round the others

parts.note: deer are animals, the plural form unchanged
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: A count of beasts found around their hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that makes you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that deadens sensation acts as an anaesthetic, making the body numb.

clue.text: One must be mad to take charge of criminal investigation

parts.note: to head something is to lead or be in charge of it
a police case is an investigation into a crime

explanation.surface: You would have to be crazy to lead an inquiry into a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Headcase is British slang for a person who is crazy or unhinged.

clue.text: Proprietor who has lost weight is a remarkable person

indicators.note: who has lost means one letter is taken out

parts.note: a proprietor is the owner of a business

explanation.surface: A shop owner who has slimmed down is quite something.
explanation.definitionFit: Oner is British slang for an outstanding or unique individual, one of a kind.

clue.text: Having midday meal at home, eating a spot of rocket

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: lunching is eating lunch at midday
pad is slang for a person's home

explanation.surface: Eating lunch at home with a bit of rocket salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket' looks like salad leaves beside lunch, but it is the space vehicle; 'a spot of' is not a little portion but a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A launching pad is the platform site from which a missile or spacecraft lifts off.

clue.text: What's reportedly stopping good young woman getting to the top?

definitions.text: What's reportedly stopping good young woman getting to the top?

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: sealing means closing off or stopping up

explanation.surface: Asking what prevents a capable woman reaching the highest posts.
explanation.walkthrough: G plus LASS, then CEILING, which 'reportedly' sounds like SEALING (stopping). The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an unseen barrier that keeps women and minorities out of senior roles at work.

clue.text: Father turning up article on character from south Pacific

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: turning means the word up is flipped round

parts.note: taken as the word itself
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Dad shows up with a piece about a figure from a South Seas musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' flips UP to PU. 'character' suggests a person in the show South Pacific, but it is someone from New Guinea.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Papua New Guinea, an island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Book — writer's account about uncle Tom's place?

parts.note: a log is a book of records, as on a ship

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A book: an author's story concerning Uncle Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NIB + AC to CABIN. Uncle Tom's Cabin is Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Tom lived in a simple timber hut, hence the jokey question mark.

clue.text: After fine start, trailed behind, tired

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of the word fine

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind

explanation.surface: After a good start, a runner falls behind and tires.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy that has flagged has weakened or drooped, as a weary person does.

clue.text: Female has compact with one in?

definitions.text: Female has compact with one in?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the others

parts.note: to pack is to press tightly together
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A woman carries a make-up compact with something inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compact' looks like a make-up case but is the verb meaning press together. Read whole, the clue pictures a woman applying a beauty treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy mask spread on the skin to cleanse it, which a woman may sit in.

clue.text: Travel costs putting off a female student

indicators.note: putting off means the named letter is removed

parts.note: fares are what passengers pay to travel
her refers to a female

explanation.surface: Ticket prices deterring a young woman at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting off' looks like deterring, but it removes A from FARES to give FRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year undergraduate at university is called a fresher in Britain.

clue.text: Relax here on cruise ship going round cape

indicators.note: going round means the outer pieces surround another

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a liner is a large passenger ship
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: Relax aboard a cruise ship as it rounds a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair with a back that tips backwards for resting in comfort.

clue.text: Discharge at end of terrible bombing raid

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of terrible

parts.note: a mission is a military operation such as a bombing sortie

explanation.surface: Bombs released at the end of a dreadful air attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpouring of gas, fluid or light, something given off.

clue.text: American guy's wife leaving hoedown, dizzy after start of jig

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind that first letter
start of picks the opening letter of jig
dizzy means spinning, so the letters are shuffled
leaving means a letter departs from the word

explanation.surface: A man's wife quits a barn dance, giddy after the first jig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes W out to give HOEDON, which 'dizzy' rearranges, placed 'after' J. The 's on guy's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The placeholder name used in the US for an unidentified or typical man.

clue.text: Soldier gets brief word of invitation to attend stag party

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: come is a word inviting someone over
a stag party is a do for men, a man do

explanation.surface: A soldier is invited to join a bachelor party.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British name for a groom's night out with male friends before his wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an elite force trained for raids is called a commando.

clue.text: Lumpy and swollen? No amount of medicine will do

parts.note: a dose is a measured quantity of a drug

explanation.surface: Bloated and bumpy: no measure of medicine will help.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodose is a technical word for knotty or having nodules.

clue.text: Given prompt, enunciated line to row at the back

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer
to row at the back means the din comes after
enunciated means spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting
din is a loud noise, a row

explanation.surface: Prompted, an actor speaks a line toward the back rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line of seats but means a racket, DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor cued in is signalled when to start speaking or entering.

clue.text: Re-enlist aid in struggle to back power of leader

indicators.note: to back means the anagram comes behind the other piece
in struggle means the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Signing up again helps the struggle to support a leader's power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in struggle' rearranges RE-ENLIST AID to RESIDENTIAL, placed 'to back' P.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidential means relating to a president, the head of a state.

clue.text: Woman performing pirouette in ballet

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin, so the letters are turned backwards
in means the letters are found inside the word ballet

explanation.surface: A female dancer spinning in a ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLE sits inside BALLET; 'performing pirouette' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's name, so stands for a woman.

clue.text: Bird, one spotted to west of British isles

indicators.note: spotted to the west means placed in front in an across answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
IS is the abbreviation for islands or isles

explanation.surface: A bird sighted off the west coast of the British Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved beak.

clue.text: Name is assigned to satellite

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: A title is given to a moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large moons of Jupiter.

clue.text: Infuriating kid in English stores

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to rag is to tease or kid

explanation.surface: A child kept inside English shops is maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb, tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Making someone furious; maddening or exasperating.
